questions.question: For $z=a+\mathrm i b$, what is $-z$?

questions.question: Which operation is easy to confuse with complex negation but is different?
options: Writing a complex number in standard form
questions.explanation: Complex conjugation ($\overline{z}=a-\mathrm{i}b$) is easily confused with negation ($-z=-a-\mathrm{i}b$), but they are different.
questions.source_support: Complex negation differs from complex conjugation.
questions.rewrite_notes: Hand-authored explanation + per-option explanations (why each wrong option is wrong + the likely misread).
option_explanations: Addition is a different operation, not easily confused with negation.

Writing $z=a+\mathrm{i}b$ in standard form is a notational choice that leaves $a$ and $b$ unchanged, whereas negation transforms $z$ into $-z=-a-\mathrm{i}b$; only conjugation $\overline{z}=a-\mathrm{i}b$ flips a single sign and is the operation genuinely confusable with negation.
Adding zero is trivial, not confusing.
